content: The primary conflict here was the classification of a villa built on shared land and properties acquired through inheritance,. The court applied the principle of accession (art. 934) and rules on inherited assets. The judge clarified that any building constructed during the marriage on a jointly owned plot automatically becomes part of the legal communion. Conversely, assets derived from an inheritance—even if finalized during the marriage—are strictly personal property and must be excluded from the division.
